title: Pobre Ana
publisher: TPRS Books (Blaine Ray Workshops); sold by Teacher's Discovery
edition: 2017 printing per the school list (Teacher's Discovery lists the current classic edition as ©2020)

sources.what: retailer product page for the classic edition: synopsis, level, word counts, present- and past-tense versions, glossary, ISBN 978-1-60372-381-7 (no chapter list)
retailer product page for the 2021 "Pobre Ana Moderna" revision (same plot, revised text and art)

summary: Blaine Ray's classic first-year TPRS novella: Ana, a 15-year-old Californian who feels her life is hard and envies her wealthier friends, spends time in Mexico with a warm host family that has less than hers, and comes home seeing her own life differently. About 250 unique words and 6,000 total words, 48 pages with a glossary; the current printing carries a present-tense version and a past-tense version under one cover.
notes: No chapter list was found on a fetched page, so the outline is empty. The school ISBN 9781603724241 (2017) is not the ISBN on the current Teacher's Discovery listing (978-1-60372-381-7, ©2020); check whether the school copy has both tense versions. A 2021 "Pobre Ana Moderna" (ISBN 978-1-7333-4643-6, with Martina Bex and Michael Coxon) keeps the plot with revised text, so a class set may mix editions. Themes: family, friendship, coming of age, wealth and poverty, life in Mexico.
